parsed.doc_summary: LAHD Relocation Assistance Bulletins A and B (rev. 7/1/2026): LA relocation assistance and filing requirements for no-fault evictions under the RSO and JCO, and for demolition for new construction under the Resident Protections Ordinance.

rules.title: LA RSO/JCO no-fault eviction relocation assistance and declaration filing
rules.requirement: Before a no-fault eviction from an RSO or JCO unit, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD, and may serve a termination notice only after filing. A copy of the notice must go to LAHD within 3 days, and the landlord must pay relocation assistance within 15 days of the notice. For 2026-27 the amounts are $11,000 to $27,400 per unit depending on tenant status and tenancy length. Low-income tenants and tenants with 3 or more years get the higher amount.
rules.key_value: $11,000-$27,400 per unit (July 1, 2026-June 30, 2027); one month's rent for qualifying single-family JCO dwellings
rules.quoted_span: All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).
rules.effective_date_note: Original effective date not stated. Current amounts are effective 2026-07-01 and increase each July 1.
rules.exemptions: No relocation is due when replacing a resident manager with another resident manager, or when a natural disaster hazard (not caused by landlord negligence) requires the eviction. Reduced amounts apply to Mom and Pop properties for owner or family occupancy evictions. Landlords may offset accumulated rent against relocation, except for government orders to vacate.
rules.penalty: Failure to file the Landlord Declaration makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO. Tenants may raise nonpayment as an affirmative defense.
rules.interaction: Applies to RSO and JCO units. Demolition for new construction of Protected Units with lower-income tenants is governed by separate RPO amounts.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family dwellings and other JCO exemptions

rules.title: LA Resident Protections Ordinance: demolition for new construction relocation and occupant protections
rules.requirement: When Protected Units are demolished for new construction, owners must pay the higher of State Housing Crisis Act or City relocation. Lower-income households receive standardized payments of $87,450 to $115,480 under Option 1. They also get a right to remain up to 6 months before construction, a 6-month notice, a right to return, and a right of first refusal.
rules.key_value: $87,450 (low), $96,750 (very low), $115,480 (extremely low) per unit under Option 1
rules.citation: L.A. Ordinance Nos. 188481 and 188482 (Resident Protections Ordinance)
rules.quoted_span: On February 11, 2025, the Los Angeles City Council adopted the RPO which codified and expanded upon replacement requirements and occupant protections of the HCA, and enhanced requirements for Restricted Affordable Units.
rules.effective_date_note: The bulletin says RPO is effective 2/11/2025 under Ordinances #188481 and #188482. It also says the Council adopted it that day.
rules.penalty: Financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.interaction: Applies only to Protected Units that will be demolished for new construction. Other units follow the regular RSO/JCO relocation rules.

requires_unknown_facts: unit is a Protected Unit (RSO unit, or rent-restricted or lower-income occupied within the past 5 years) being demolished for new construction
